'''Ira Reynolds Newble II''' (born January 20, 1975) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[San Antonio Spurs]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Seattle SuperSonics]], and [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

==College career==
After graduating from [[Southfield High School]] in 1993, Newble went to [[Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College]] before attending [[Miami University]] in Ohio, where he studied sports marketing. As a senior at Miami, he averaged 11.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 1.2 assists per game while earning Honorable Mention All-[[Mid-American Conference]] honors.

==Professional career==

===Early career===
Newble played for three seasons in the [[International Basketball Association]] (IBA) and later the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) before playing in 2000 overseas. He also played stints in the CBA in 2001 and the [[United States Basketball League]] (USBL) in 2002.

===NBA career===
Newble signed as a free agent with the NBA's [[San Antonio Spurs]] and his NBA debut with in the 2000–2001 season, playing in 27 games, of which he started six. In just under seven minutes per game, he averaged 2.0 points per game (ppg) and 1.3 rebounds per game (rpg).<ref name="basketball-reference.com">{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/newblir01.html| title = Ira Newble Stats {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> He was waived by the Spurs after the season.

He then signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the 2001–2002 season, and his playing time and production greatly increased. Playing 42 games (starting 35), he played over 30 minutes per game, averaging 8.0 ppg and 5.3 rpg, which would both be career highs for Newble. On April 13, 2002, against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Newble set a then career single-game high with 17 points and a career-high 12 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/newblir01/gamelog/2002/| title = Ira Newble 2001-02 Game Log {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> The following season, 2002–03, he played in 73 games (starting 45), averaging 7.7 ppg, 3.7 rpg, and a career-high 1.4 assists per game.<ref name="basketball-reference.com"/> On April 12, 2003, he set a career personal-best with 21 points against the [[Washington Wizards]], then topped that two days later with 23 against the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/n/newblir01/gamelog/2003/| title = Ira Newble 2002-03 Game Log {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

The Cleveland Cavaliers signed Newble as a free agent in July 2003. In the 2003–04 season, in 64 games (25 as a starter) playing about 19 minutes per game, he averaged 4.0 ppg and 2.4 rpg. In 2004–05, he played a career-high 74 games (starting a career-high 69), averaging 5.9 ppg and 3.0 rpg.<ref name="basketball-reference.com"/>

Injuries hampered Newble in the [[2005–06 NBA season]]. He missed 21 games with a right foot strain and missed 14 games with a facial abscess, limiting him to 36 games. In 2006–07, he was limited to only 15 games. In 2007–08, he bounced back, playing in 41 games for the Cavs then, on February 21, 2008, he was traded to the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in a multi-player deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/transactions/feb2008_transactions.html |title=NBA.com: February 2008 Transactions |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2008-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080727013735/http://www.nba.com/transactions/feb2008_transactions.html |archive-date=2008-07-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived by the Sonics one week later after playing just two games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/sonics/#/news/archive/article_roster080229 Sonics Roster Updates]</ref> In the [[2006–07 NBA season]] he was a part of the team that won the Eastern Conference Championship.

In March, 2008, Newble signed a 10-day contract with the Los Angeles Lakers.<ref>[http://www.latimes.com/sports/printedition/la-sp-lakerep22mar22,1,7720962.story Lakers sign Ira Newble]</ref> Nine days later, the Lakers signed Newble for the remainder of the season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/080401newblesigned.html Lakers Sign Ira Newble For Remainder Of Season]</ref> He played six games for the Lakers, ending his eight-year NBA career with 1,930 points, 1,114 rebounds, 342 assists, 204 steals and 105 blocks in 380 games.<ref name="basketball-reference.com"/>

===European career===
Newble started his professional career overseas in the [[Cyprus Basketball Division 1|Cypriot League]] playing for [[Keravnos B.C.|Keravnos Strovolos]]. Keravnos won the [[Cyprus Basketball Division 1]] championship in 2000.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.eurobasket.com/team.asp?Cntry=CYPRUS&Team=707&Page=5| title = Keravnos Strovolou basketball, News, Roster, Rumors, Stats, Awards, Transactions, Details-eurobasket}}</ref> In March 2009, he signed with [[Bnei HaSharon]] from the Israeli [[Israeli Basketball Super League|BSL]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europa/esteri/956/bnei_hasharon_newble_to_replace_onyekwe.html |title=Bnei Hasharon, Newble to replace Onyekwe |access-date=2009-04-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724082015/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europa/esteri/956/bnei_hasharon_newble_to_replace_onyekwe.html |archive-date=2011-07-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He joined the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek League]] club [[Aris BC|Aris Thessaloniki]] in August 2009.<ref>[http://www.arisbc.gr/index.php?SCREEN=page&PageID=2152&LangID=1 Arisbc.gr πό τα κίτρινα των Lakers, στα κίτρινα του ΑΡΗ o IRA NEWBLE {{in lang|el}}]</ref>  He signed for [[Cáceres Ciudad del Baloncesto|Cáceres 2016 Basket]] in December 2009.<ref name="Caceres 2016">[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europa/esteri/5162/ira_newble_signs_for_caceres_2016.html Ira Newble signs for Caceres 2016]</ref> Cáceres released him a month later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Caceres replace Ira Newble with Shawn Taggart|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2010/1/24.asp|publisher=Eurobasket|access-date=June 6, 2011|date=January 24, 2010}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
In 2011, Newble became an assistant coach of the [[Canton Charge]], the new [[NBA Development League]] affiliate of Newble's former team Cleveland Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Weir|first=Josh|title=Newble returns to the court as coach with Charge|url=http://www.cantonrep.com/charge/x1440922325/Newble-returns-to-the-court-as-coach-with-Charge|work=CantonRep.com|access-date=May 11, 2012|date=March 31, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404042307/http://www.cantonrep.com/charge/x1440922325/Newble-returns-to-the-court-as-coach-with-Charge|archive-date=April 4, 2012}}</ref>

In 2012, Newble became an assistant coach for the [[Austin Toros]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. He would continue to coach for the Toros under their last two seasons in that name before being renamed to the [[Austin Spurs]]. On October 31, 2015, he became an assistant coach for the [[Bakersfield Jam]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bakersfield Jam Announce 2015-16 Staff|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065106|access-date=October 31, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 30, 2015}}</ref>

== Darfur campaign ==
In 2007, Newble led a campaign to help bring awareness to China's involvement in the [[war in Darfur]] as a weapons supplier.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aidstillrequired.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/03/Associated_Press6-15-08.pdf|title=Lakers forward Ira Newble takes stand on Darfur conflict|agency=[[Associated Press|AP]]|publisher=[[Aid Still Required]]|date=June 15, 2008|access-date=May 15, 2025}}</ref> Newble saw a letter that [[Aid Still Required]] had written expressing concern about investments funding the crisis. He collected signatures around the league for the letter that then was presented to the Chinese government and the President of the [[Olympic Committee]] for the [[2008 Summer Olympic Games]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aolsportsblog.com/2007/05/10/cavs-newble-takes-up-darfur-cause/ |title=Cavs' Newble Takes Up Darfur Cause – FanHouse – AOL Sports Blog<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=May 12, 2007 |archive-date=May 13, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070513043857/http://www.aolsportsblog.com/2007/05/10/cavs-newble-takes-up-darfur-cause/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
